All saved. Here's the wrap-up:

## What was built — `D:\physics\sdft`

An **on-policy SDFT pipeline** for distilling the `armand0e/qwen3.7-max-pi-traces` agent traces into an open model without destructive SFT. Since qwen3.7-max is API-only (no logits), the **model is its own teacher**: the frozen base conditioned on the expert turn injected in-context scores the student's *own rollouts*, and training minimizes exact full-vocab per-token reverse KL. No cross-entropy on off-policy tokens anywhere. With LoRA, the teacher is the adapter-disabled base — zero extra weight memory.

- `sdft/` — trace parser (teich JSONL → normalized messages), prompt/target rendering, batched rollouts, chunked KL with a **closed-form reverse-KL backward** (`p·(r−KL)/T`, recomputed in backward — saves ~2 GB at Qwen's 248k vocab, gradient verified against autograd to 6e-8)
- `scripts/` — `prepare_data.py`, `inspect_data.py`, `train_sdft.py`, `vram_probe.py`
- `configs/` — Qwen3-8B default, Qwen3.5-9B, two smoke configs, pi tool schemas
- `data/examples.jsonl` — 1,234 per-turn examples ready to train (median context ~33k tokens, p90 ~94k, max ~142k)

**Verified on your machine:** both smoke tests pass end-to-end on CUDA (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B — multimodal class, rollouts, teacher scoring, optimizer step, checkpoint save); the Qwen3.5 adapter provably contains **zero vision-tower tensors** (multimodal retention by construction); 4-bit QLoRA loading is wired in.

## Your 16 GB question (estimates — the 4B probe never ran)

**4B should be your target, not 0.8B.** My best estimates with the memory-efficient KL:

| Model (bf16 LoRA) | Context budget on 16 GB | Dataset coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-0.8B (1.7 GB weights) | ~96k | ~90% |
| Qwen3.5-2B (4.4 GB) | ~32–48k | ~50–65% |
| Qwen3.5-4B (9.1 GB) | ~12–16k | ~25–30% |
| Qwen3.5-4B **QLoRA 4-bit** (~3.5 GB) | ~24–32k | ~50% |

**Critical caveat I found before stopping:** at 12k context the 4B OOM'd — not from the model, but because transformers builds a float attention mask for this multimodal arch even on text-only input, and SDPA backward then allocates a `(heads, T, T)` fp32 buffer (9.77 GiB at T=12.8k). I wrote `sdft/patches.py` (`attn_implementation: sdpa_textonly`) that drops the mask for text-only batches — wired into the trainer and probe but **untested**, since your GPU got busy.

## Notes for when you pick this up

1. **First step:** `python scripts/vram_probe.py --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --prompt-tokens 12288 --resp-tokens 512` (weights are already in your HF cache). It replicates one full training step and reports per-phase peak VRAM. Then binary-search your real context ceiling.
2. **Speed on Windows is the bigger problem than memory:** the DeltaNet layers run a slow torch fallback because the fast path needs both `flash-linear-attention` (installed, 0.5.0) *and* `causal-conv1d` (CUDA extension, painful to build on Windows). **WSL2 would fix all of it** — fla, causal-conv1d, flash-attn, and vLLM for fast rollouts all install cleanly there, on the same GPU.
3. Watch `kl_per_token` during training — near zero means the student matches the expert without the demonstration in context. Set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` to reduce fragmentation on a tight card.
4. Everything above plus the attention pitfall is saved to memory, so future sessions will pick up where this left off.
